reviews.rationale: Hos.1.1 is the book's complete provenance heading: the word-event and regnal synchronisms finish before the narrated first-command formula in 1:2. Joining 1:2 would erase a clear form change from superscription to enacted-sign commission.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.1.1-Hos.1.2: That span would merge the paratext-like prophetic heading with the first enacted-sign command even though Hos.1.2 supplies a new temporal formula, reported speech, and imperative scene.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.1.1-Hos.1.2: That span would merge the paratext-like prophetic heading with the first enacted-sign command even though Hos.1.2 supplies a new temporal formula, reported speech, and imperative scene.

reviews.rationale: The three conception-birth-naming cycles accumulate as one enacted family sign through 1:9, where the paired WLC-family sources place a samekh. Internal navigation may expose each name, but top-level separation would overstate three seams unsupported by the source layout.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.1.2a|Hos.1.2b: the midverse pe distinguishes frame from speech but does not make either fragment a useful independent retrieval unit.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.1.2a|Hos.1.2b: the midverse pe distinguishes frame from speech but does not make either fragment a useful independent retrieval unit.

reviews.rationale: The reversal beginning at 1:10 runs across the English chapter edge through 2:1: innumerability, reunification, one head, Jezreel, 'my people,' and 'loved one' answer the prior names. The imperative lawsuit reset at 2:2 closes this coherent counter-oracle.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.1.10-Hos.1.11; Hos.2.1: the final imperatives enact the same name reversal and would become a one-verse orphan.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.1.10-Hos.1.11; Hos.2.1: the final imperatives enact the same name reversal and would become a one-verse orphan.

reviews.rationale: The doubled 'Contend' begins one accusation-to-consequence lawsuit in 2:2-13; lover pursuit, blocked path, withdrawn gifts, ended festivals, ruined crops, and the Baal conclusion are causally chained. A split at 2:5 would detach consequence from charge.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.2.2-Hos.2.7 and Hos.2.8-Hos.2.13: The second half supplies the reason and enacted consequences of the first; splitting would weaken the complete accusation-to-consequence lawsuit movement.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.2.2-Hos.2.7 and Hos.2.8-Hos.2.13: The second half supplies the reason and enacted consequences of the first; splitting would weaken the complete accusation-to-consequence lawsuit movement.

reviews.rationale: The wilderness allurement at 2:14 opens the restoration answer that proceeds through renamed relation, peace, betrothal, creation's response, and reversal of the child names at 2:23. Several internal markers compete, so none warrants severing this complete response movement.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.2.14-Hos.2.20 and Hos.2.21-Hos.2.23: The cosmic response and sowing/name reversal are the harvest of the preceding restored relationship and should hydrate as the same promise movement.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.2.14-Hos.2.20 and Hos.2.21-Hos.2.23: The cosmic response and sowing/name reversal are the harvest of the preceding restored relationship and should hydrate as the same promise movement.

reviews.rationale: Chapter 3 is one enacted restoration sign: command, acquisition, direct instruction, and the explanatory without/afterward contrast resolve together at 3:5. Dividing the action from its interpretation would leave both halves rhetorically incomplete.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.3.1-Hos.3.3 and Hos.3.4-Hos.3.5: The latter verses explicitly interpret the duration and direction of the enacted sign; detaching them would reduce both narrative and oracle coherence.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.3.1-Hos.3.3 and Hos.3.4-Hos.3.5: The latter verses explicitly interpret the duration and direction of the enacted sign; detaching them would reduce both narrative and oracle coherence.

reviews.rationale: The hearing summons and explicit charge in 4:1 develop through a compact offence catalogue into land-and-creature mourning at 4:3. The countercharge against disputants in 4:4 changes the addressee and argumentative posture, establishing the next seam.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.4.1-Hos.4.2 and Hos.4.3: Hos.4.3 is the expressly signaled consequence of the charges and would become an orphan ecological image if separated.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.4.1-Hos.4.2 and Hos.4.3: Hos.4.3 is the expressly signaled consequence of the charges and would become an orphan ecological image if separated.

reviews.rationale: Hos.4.4-10 turns from the land charge to priest-people knowledge failure and reciprocal rejection, moving through multiplication, shame, sin-feeding, punishment, and frustrated appetite. The vice maxim at 4:11 begins a new cultic-intoxication cluster.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.4.4-Hos.4.6 and Hos.4.7-Hos.4.10: Hos.4.7-4.10 develops the same priestly rejection into shame, appetite, and reciprocal punishment; the internal stanza is better retained under one parent unit.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.4.4-Hos.4.6 and Hos.4.7-Hos.4.10: Hos.4.7-4.10 develops the same priestly rejection into shame, appetite, and reciprocal punishment; the internal stanza is better retained under one parent unit.

reviews.rationale: Prostitution, wine, divination, hill worship, and the responsibility reversal concerning daughters form the tightly linked cultic accusation of 4:11-14. The concessive address to Israel and direct prohibitions concerning Judah at 4:15 create the stronger seam.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.4.11-Hos.4.12 and Hos.4.13-Hos.4.14: The mountain practices are the concrete expansion of the preceding divination/infidelity charge, and the final lack-of-understanding verdict closes the opening maxim.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.4.11-Hos.4.12 and Hos.4.13-Hos.4.14: The mountain practices are the concrete expansion of the preceding divination/infidelity charge, and the final lack-of-understanding verdict closes the opening maxim.

reviews.rationale: Hos.4.15-19 is a direct warning sequence: negative imperatives, stubborn-heifer question, Ephraim's idol verdict, sour drink, and wind-borne shame. The samekh after 4:19 corroborates closure before the triadic leadership summons in 5:1.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.4.15-Hos.4.17 and Hos.4.18-Hos.4.19: The drink and wind couplet concludes the same Ephraim-idol warning; a two-verse image split would over-weight metaphor changes over the continuing verdict.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.4.15-Hos.4.17 and Hos.4.18-Hos.4.19: The drink and wind couplet concludes the same Ephraim-idol warning; a two-verse image split would over-weight metaphor changes over the continuing verdict.

reviews.rationale: The threefold summons to priests, Israel, and the royal house opens 5:1-7 and governs the snare, defilement, failed seeking, and new-moon sentence. The samekh after 5:7 and trumpet imperatives at 5:8 jointly establish a robust boundary.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.5.1-Hos.5.3 and Hos.5.4-Hos.5.7: The deeds, pride, stumbling, and failed seeking are the consequence movement of the leadership summons rather than a new oracle.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.5.1-Hos.5.3 and Hos.5.4-Hos.5.7: The deeds, pride, stumbling, and failed seeking are the consequence movement of the leadership summons rather than a new oracle.

reviews.rationale: The alarm calls of 5:8 initiate an escalating battle-and-sickness oracle that ends with divine withdrawal in 5:15. The communal first-person invitation 'Come, let us return' at 6:1 is a speaker and form reset rather than a continuation of the alarm.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.5.8-Hos.5.12 and Hos.5.13-Hos.5.15: The foreign-healing episode and lion judgment complete the sickness/decay trajectory introduced in Hos.5.11-5.12; splitting would obscure the escalation.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.5.8-Hos.5.12 and Hos.5.13-Hos.5.15: The foreign-healing episode and lion judgment complete the sickness/decay trajectory introduced in Hos.5.11-5.12; splitting would obscure the escalation.

reviews.rationale: Hos.6.1-3 is a compact communal return summons built from imperatives, tearing/healing confidence, two/three-day language, and rain imagery. The direct divine Ephraim/Judah questions in 6:4 answer and reframe it, so the speech remains distinct without deciding its sincerity.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.5.15-Hos.6.3: Hos.5.15 is divine first-person withdrawal, while Hos.6.1 begins an overt first-person plural quoted response; preserving adjacent units retains the call-and-response seam without conflating voices.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.5.15-Hos.6.3: Hos.5.15 is divine first-person withdrawal, while Hos.6.1 begins an overt first-person plural quoted response; preserving adjacent units retains the call-and-response seam without conflating voices.

reviews.rationale: The divine questions in 6:4 lead through transient loyalty, prophetic cutting, mercy/knowledge, covenant breach, and localized blood accusation to Judah's harvest in 6:11. A correlated pe follows 6:11; therefore the 6:11-7:2 syntax is preserved as an overlay, not substituted for the route boundary.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.6.4-Hos.6.7; Hos.6.8-Hos.6.11: A plausible aphorism-plus-local-indictment child route, rejected as primary because the betrayal theme and divine response continue.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.6.4-Hos.6.7; Hos.6.8-Hos.6.11: A plausible aphorism-plus-local-indictment child route, rejected as primary because the betrayal theme and divine response continue.

reviews.rationale: The attempted-healing formula in 7:1 exposes iniquity and develops through remembered deeds, royal complicity, and the oven-court portrait to fallen kings in 7:7. Splitting at 7:2 or 7:3 would detach the exposure from its social and royal outworking.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.7.1-Hos.7.3; Hos.7.4-Hos.7.7: Rejected as the primary route because falsehood, royal complicity, and oven conspiracy make one movement; retain as possible children.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.7.1-Hos.7.3; Hos.7.4-Hos.7.7: Rejected as the primary route because falsehood, royal complicity, and oven conspiracy make one movement; retain as possible children.

reviews.rationale: The cake, consumed strength, unnoticed gray hair, pride, dove-like foreign appeal, and divine net form one failed-awareness and foreign-orientation movement in 7:8-12. The samekh after 7:12 supplies firmer closure than the image-only proposal at 7:10.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.7.8-Hos.7.10; Hos.7.11-Hos.7.12: Rejected as primary units because the whole sequence depicts failed awareness and foreign orientation before divine interception.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.7.8-Hos.7.10; Hos.7.11-Hos.7.12: Rejected as primary units because the whole sequence depicts failed awareness and foreign orientation before divine interception.

reviews.rationale: The woe at 7:13 opens a renewed lament-accusation: wandering, false speech, bed-howling, grain assembly, divine strengthening, and faulty return conclude at 7:16. Retaining 7:11-16 would ignore the source-backed closure after 7:12.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.7.13-Hos.7.15; Hos.7.16: the final bow/prince/Egypt line concludes the false-return accusation and should not become an orphan.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.7.13-Hos.7.15; Hos.7.16: the final bow/prince/Egypt line concludes the false-return accusation and should not become an orphan.

reviews.rationale: The trumpet command in 8:1 launches covenant-law accusation, false acknowledgement, unauthorized rulers, and the Samaria calf rebuttal through 8:6. The sowing proverb at 8:7 begins consequences rather than merely extending the calf description.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.8.1-Hos.8.3 and Hos.8.4-Hos.8.6: The unauthorized kings and made calf specify how the covenant/law rebellion contradicts the acknowledgment cry; keeping the rebuttal together is more coherent.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.8.1-Hos.8.3 and Hos.8.4-Hos.8.6: The unauthorized kings and made calf specify how the covenant/law rebellion contradicts the acknowledgment cry; keeping the rebuttal together is more coherent.

reviews.rationale: Hos.8.7-10 develops sowing and whirlwind into failed crop, swallowing among nations, Assyrian movement, hired lovers, and gathering. The repeated altar accusation at 8:11 resets the subject and begins the cult-law unit.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.8.7 and Hos.8.8-Hos.8.10: The famous sow/reap line introduces the entire swallowing consequence chain and should not be isolated as a proverb-sized proof-text.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.8.7 and Hos.8.8-Hos.8.10: The famous sow/reap line introduces the entire swallowing consequence chain and should not be isolated as a proverb-sized proof-text.

reviews.rationale: Multiplied altars, disregarded written instruction, rejected sacrifice, remembered guilt, Egypt, palaces, and fortifications form the coherent indictment of 8:11-14. The samekh after 8:14 confirms closure before the festival prohibition in 9:1.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.8.11-Hos.8.13 and Hos.8.14: Hos.8.14's 'For Israel has forgotten' supplies the concluding reason and broadens the same cultic-memory indictment to building and fire; it is not a detached Judah oracle.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.8.11-Hos.8.13 and Hos.8.14: Hos.8.14's 'For Israel has forgotten' supplies the concluding reason and broadens the same cultic-memory indictment to building and fire; it is not a detached Judah oracle.

reviews.rationale: The prohibition on rejoicing governs 9:1-6 as threshing-floor, land, food, sacrifice, feast, flight, burial, and ruined-tent consequences unfold. The doubled 'days have come' formula at 9:7 introduces a visitation and watchman stanza.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.9.1-Hos.9.4 and Hos.9.5-Hos.9.6: The feast-day question and burial answer complete the festival warning; separation would leave the question without the preceding loss of acceptable worship.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.9.1-Hos.9.4 and Hos.9.5-Hos.9.6: The feast-day question and burial answer complete the festival warning; separation would leave the question without the preceding loss of acceptable worship.

reviews.rationale: Days of visitation and reckoning, hostility toward prophet/watchman, snare imagery, and the Gibeah verdict make 9:7-9 a compact stanza closed by a samekh. Speaker identity remains unassigned, but that meaning question does not convert this accepted boundary into a hold.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.9.7-Hos.9.8 and Hos.9.9: Hos.9.9 supplies the historical-comparative verdict and punishment closure for the hostility/snare stanza; the boundary is accepted while only internal speaker and lineation presentation remains unresolved.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.9.7-Hos.9.8 and Hos.9.9: Hos.9.9 supplies the historical-comparative verdict and punishment closure for the hostility/snare stanza; the boundary is accepted while only internal speaker and lineation presentation remains unresolved.

reviews.rationale: The wilderness-grape recollection at 9:10 turns through Baal Peor, vanished glory, lost birth, bereavement, and the petition at 9:14. Gilgal in 9:15 relocates and restarts the accusation, so the anguished petition closes this fertility lament.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.9.10-Hos.9.13 and Hos.9.14: The one-verse petition voices the preceding bereavement crisis and should not be atomized; its interruption is a climactic lament turn inside the same movement.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.9.10-Hos.9.13 and Hos.9.14: The one-verse petition voices the preceding bereavement crisis and should not be atomized; its interruption is a climactic lament turn inside the same movement.

reviews.rationale: Gilgal wickedness, expulsion, dried root, lost fruit, and the prophetic wandering coda belong together in 9:15-17 despite the surface voice change at 9:17. The two adjacent WLC-family samekhs mark internal layout and final closure, not an orphaned one-verse chunk.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.9.15-Hos.9.16 and Hos.9.17: Although Hos.9.17 changes the surface speaker, it is a short summarizing coda that repeats rejection and gives the oracle its final wandering consequence.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.9.15-Hos.9.16 and Hos.9.17: Although Hos.9.17 changes the surface speaker, it is a short summarizing coda that repeats rejection and gives the oracle its final wandering consequence.

reviews.rationale: The luxuriant vine begins a cult-monarchy poem that moves through altars, divided heart, kinglessness, false covenant, calf deportation, and destroyed high places to the mountains/hills cry in 10:8. The samekh there closes the full movement.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.10.1-Hos.10.4 and Hos.10.5-Hos.10.8: The calf and high-place collapse are the concrete cultic consequence of the vine/altar and false-covenant diagnosis; the macro sequence should remain retrievable as one.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.10.1-Hos.10.4 and Hos.10.5-Hos.10.8: The calf and high-place collapse are the concrete cultic consequence of the vine/altar and false-covenant diagnosis; the macro sequence should remain retrievable as one.

reviews.rationale: Gibeah recollection in 10:9-10 proceeds into heifer and field imagery, an appeal to sow righteousness, the reversal of wicked plowing, and battle devastation through 10:15. A split at 10:10 would sever recollection from the appeal-consequence triptych.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.10.9-Hos.10.11, Hos.10.12, and Hos.10.13-Hos.10.15: Isolating the famous sow-in-righteousness verse would destroy the designed contrast between the appeal and the immediately reversed plowing/reaping judgment.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.10.9-Hos.10.11, Hos.10.12, and Hos.10.13-Hos.10.15: Isolating the famous sow-in-righteousness verse would destroy the designed contrast between the appeal and the immediately reversed plowing/reaping judgment.

reviews.rationale: Parental recollection in 11:1-4 and refusal/Assyria consequence in 11:5-7 are causally interlocked: calling, teaching, healing, love, and feeding are rejected before sword and failed return. A smaller citation-shaped child at 11:1-4 is therefore not activated.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.11.1-Hos.11.4 and Hos.11.5-Hos.11.7: The consequence stanza is the direct reversal of the parental care recollection; retaining the full movement avoids sentimental proof-texting of either half.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.11.1-Hos.11.4 and Hos.11.5-Hos.11.7: The consequence stanza is the direct reversal of the parental care recollection; retaining the full movement avoids sentimental proof-texting of either half.

reviews.rationale: The repeated compassion questions at 11:8 turn from threatened surrender to restrained anger, divine self-description, lion-like call, trembling return, and settlement through 11:11. A samekh at the close distinguishes this promise from the renewed accusation in 11:12.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.11.8-Hos.11.9 and Hos.11.10-Hos.11.11: The returning children are the narrative consequence of the compassion/restraint question chain, so the judgment-restoration turn should stay whole.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.11.8-Hos.11.9 and Hos.11.10-Hos.11.11: The returning children are the narrative consequence of the compassion/restraint question chain, so the judgment-restoration turn should stay whole.

reviews.rationale: Falsehood at 11:12 continues into wind, lies, Assyria, and Egypt at 12:1; local 12:2 then opens an explicit controversy and Jacob recollection ending in the return appeal at 12:6. The rib formula is a real internal seam, but the two-verse bridge is not yet safe as an autonomous retrieval object, so the larger unit is held.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.11.12-Hos.12.1 plus Hos.12.2-Hos.12.6: The controversy formula at local Hos.12.2 is a genuine internal seam, but the short bridge remains unsafe as an autonomous retrieval object because the Judah clause, speaker relation, and shifted MT coordinates remain contested; the larger unit is retained pending external-model and human review.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.11.12-Hos.12.1 plus Hos.12.2-Hos.12.6: The controversy formula at local Hos.12.2 is a genuine internal seam, but the short bridge remains unsafe as an autonomous retrieval object because the Judah clause, speaker relation, and shifted MT coordinates remain contested; the larger unit is retained pending external-model and human review.

reviews.rationale: The merchant/scale accusation and wealth boast in 12:7-8 receive a divine Egypt, tents, prophets, visions, and altar rebuttal through 12:11. The Jacob-in-Aram comparison at 12:12 begins a fresh parallel, making 12:7-11 the complete accusation-response unit.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.12.7-Hos.12.8 and Hos.12.9-Hos.12.11: The divine self-identification and tent/prophet/altar sequence is the direct rebuttal to the wealth-and-innocence boast; separating accusation from answer weakens the dialogue.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.12.7-Hos.12.8 and Hos.12.9-Hos.12.11: The divine self-identification and tent/prophet/altar sequence is the direct rebuttal to the wealth-and-innocence boast; separating accusation from answer weakens the dialogue.

reviews.rationale: Jacob's service for a wife and a prophet-mediated exodus form the paired ancestral-prophetic recollection of 12:12-13, answered by the repayment verdict in 12:14. Separating the verdict would strip the comparison of its stated consequence.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.12.12-Hos.12.13 and Hos.12.14: Hos.12.14 supplies the verdict against which the paired recollections function; detaching it would leave the comparison rhetorically unresolved.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.12.12-Hos.12.13 and Hos.12.14: Hos.12.14 supplies the verdict against which the paired recollections function; detaching it would leave the comparison rhetorically unresolved.

reviews.rationale: Ephraim's rise, Baal-linked death, intensified image-making, and four vanishing similes form the compressed history and verdict of 13:1-3. Direct divine self-identification and exodus recollection at 13:4 reset both voice and temporal field.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.13.1-Hos.13.2 and Hos.13.3: Hos.13.3 is the expressly marked consequence of the rise-to-idolatry accusation and should not be isolated as an image anthology.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.13.1-Hos.13.2 and Hos.13.3: Hos.13.3 is the expressly marked consequence of the rise-to-idolatry accusation and should not be isolated as an image anthology.

reviews.rationale: The exodus-provider recollection in 13:4-6 reverses into forgetting and a predator sequence in 13:7-8, linked by repeated causal language. Dividing provision from the animal judgment would obscure the accusation-to-consequence structure.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.13.4-Hos.13.6 and Hos.13.7-Hos.13.8: The predator judgment is the explicit 'Therefore' reversal of provision and forgetting; keeping provider-to-predator movement prevents proof-texting either image field.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.13.4-Hos.13.6 and Hos.13.7-Hos.13.8: The predator judgment is the explicit 'Therefore' reversal of provision and forgetting; keeping provider-to-predator movement prevents proof-texting either image field.

reviews.rationale: The helper statement and king/judge questions in 13:9-10 are answered by the anger-and-wrath verdict in 13:11. A samekh after 13:11 closes the monarchy cluster before stored guilt begins at 13:12.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.13.9 and Hos.13.10-Hos.13.11: The helper/save contrast introduces the king's inability to save, so Hos.13.9 is the rhetorical premise of the question-answer unit.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.13.9 and Hos.13.10-Hos.13.11: The helper/save contrast introduces the king's inability to save, so Hos.13.9 is the rhetorical premise of the question-answer unit.

reviews.rationale: Stored guilt, failed birth, the Death/Sheol address, hidden compassion, east wind, dried source, plunder, and Samaria's sentence run continuously through local 13:16. Because no pinned marker supports 13:14|13:15 and punctuation remains contested, the larger unit is retained as a genuine external-review hold.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.13.12-Hos.13.14; Hos.13.15-Hos.13.16: Serious death-address/east-wind alternative rejected provisionally because birth, death, east wind, and terminal destruction form one compressed judgment movement.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.13.12-Hos.13.14; Hos.13.15-Hos.13.16: Serious death-address/east-wind alternative rejected provisionally because birth, death, east wind, and terminal destruction form one compressed judgment movement.

reviews.rationale: The imperative 'Return' at 14:1 opens a supplied communal confession: take words, ask forgiveness, renounce Assyria, horses, and handmade gods, and appeal to mercy through 14:3. The first-person healing answer in 14:4 changes speaker and form.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.14.1 and Hos.14.2-Hos.14.3: Hos.14.1's return command is immediately elaborated by 'Take words ... and return'; separating it would atomize the summons from the prayer it supplies.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.14.1 and Hos.14.2-Hos.14.3: Hos.14.1's return command is immediately elaborated by 'Take words ... and return'; separating it would atomize the summons from the prayer it supplies.

reviews.rationale: Divine healing and freely given love in 14:4 unfold through dew, lily, Lebanon, olive, shade, grain, vine, and the idol/fruit capstone at 14:8. The internal samekh before local 14:8 is recorded, but speaker and verbal-force uncertainty make a one-verse child unsafe.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.14.4-Hos.14.7 and Hos.14.8-Hos.14.9: Hos.14.8 remains divine first-person speech and completes the idol-to-fruit answer, whereas Hos.14.9 alone has the wisdom question and righteous/rebellious contrast; the proposed alternative crosses the sharper form seam.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.14.4-Hos.14.7 and Hos.14.8-Hos.14.9: Hos.14.8 remains divine first-person speech and completes the idol-to-fruit answer, whereas Hos.14.9 alone has the wisdom question and righteous/rebellious contrast; the proposed alternative crosses the sharper form seam.

reviews.rationale: The generalized 'Who is wise?' questions in 14:9 turn from the preceding dialogue to the reader and summarize the book as ways walked or stumbled in. This wisdom colophon is formally self-contained while still requiring whole-book hydration.
reviews.counterevidence: Hos.14.4-Hos.14.9: Merging the colophon would erase the demonstrable shift from direct divine promise and first-person imagery to generalized wisdom address; this one-verse unit is form-driven, not fame-driven.
reviews.rejected_alternative: Hos.14.4-Hos.14.9: Merging the colophon would erase the demonstrable shift from direct divine promise and first-person imagery to generalized wisdom address; this one-verse unit is form-driven, not fame-driven.
